Break-away ice buoys reveal changes in Antarctic sea ice
FEIT researchers Dr Joey Voermans and Professor Alexander Babanin from the Department of Infrastructure Engineering, together with Dr Petra Heil from the British Antarctic Survey and other collaborators, have studied the impact of waves generated inside areas of open water amid Antarctic sea ice can become energetic enough to break up sea ice from the inside out.

Infrastructure Engineering Graduate Research Conference 2026
The annual Infrastructure Engineering Graduate Research Conference (IEGRC) for 2026, was held on the 28th of September at the Rydges Hotel in Melbourne.The event was organised by the 2026 Graduates' Infrastructure Engineering Society (GIES) and supported by the Department of Infrastructure Engineering.Mr. Geoffrey Ferres (Global Alliance Executive-AI Solutions) from EY Australia delivered the keynote address on planning ahead for intelligent infrastructure.Over 70 graduate researchers successfully presented their research covering disciplines in structural engineering, geotechnical engineering, hydrology & water, geomatics & transportation, and multidisciplinary engineering (engineering management, ocean engineering, energy and indigenous engineering).Thank you to the GIES committee, staff, and volunteers for making it another successful event.
